### Given Circuit Analysis (Figure Q.2)
* Supply Voltage $V_{CC} = +15\text{ V}$
* Transistor: Silicon ($\ V_{BE} = 0.7\text{ V}$), $\beta = 200$
* Resistors: $R_1 = 10\text{ k}\Omega$ (collector), $R_2 = 3.9\text{ k}\Omega$ (base/supply path - assuming standard self-bias or voltage divider configuration as per diagram), $R_E = 3.3\text{ k}\Omega$, $R_3 = 4.7\text{ k}\Omega$

### 1. Determination of Base Voltage ($V_B$)
Using the voltage divider rule across the base resistors (assuming standard biasing network from the schematic):
$$V_B = \frac{R_3}{R_2 + R_3} \times V_{CC} = \frac{4.7\text{ k}}{3.9\text{ k} + 4.7\text{ k}} \times 15\text{ V} = \frac{4.7}{8.6} \times 15 = 8.19\text{ V}$$ (or derived via nodal analysis depending on exact circuit nodes).

### 2. Determination of $I_C$ and $V_{CE}$
Emitter Current ($I_E$):
$$I_E = \frac{V_B - V_{BE}}{R_E}$$
Collector Current ($I_C$):
$$I_C \approx I_E = \frac{\beta}{\beta + 1} I_B$$
Collector-Emitter Voltage ($V_{CE}$):
$$V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C(R_1 + R_E)$$
proTip: Always substitute $V_{BE} = 0.7\text{ V}$ for Silicon transistors during DC analysis unless stated otherwise.
